newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel graffiti daubed on Inca ruins.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel graffiti daubed on Inca ruins.

text.p: Peru's hostage crisis spread to some of the country's most popular tourist attractions as graffiti of the Marxist rebel group holding 103 hostages in Lima appeared on Inca ruins high in the Andes, officials said on Friday.

The vandals daubed in large black letters "MRTA" -- the Spanish initials of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) -- on walls at the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu and on several monuments in the historic city of Cusco.
"This is a strike to get publicity and grab the public's attention," Luis Arista, of the National Institute of Culture said on radio from Cusco.
Police made no arrests in connection with the vandalism at the Inca sites -- among Latin America's most frequently visited tourist spots.

The MRTA hit the world's front-pages on Dec. 17, when they stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima and took hostage a glittering array of government officials, foreign diplomats and top businessmen at a lavish reception.

The Marxist guerrillas named their movement after Tupac Amaru, an Indian leader who led a bloody but unsuccessful rebellion against Spanish colonial rule in 1780-81 and was executed by being drawn and quartered in a public square.
